doc: Deferred negatives (debt D7 -- docs/verdict_policy.md Section 6). Positive cases whose verdict guard IS expect-flippable (it compares against an operator-supplied expected value) but which carry no sound NEG_ROW yet, each with an explicit reason. Unlike the conformant-absence registry (DUT-behaviour guards that no --expect can fault), these can and should eventually get a sound expect-flip negative or a parameterisation; the reason records why they don't yet (Linux deviation makes the positive itself fail, the guard checks a compiled constant that must be lifted to applyExpectedDefaults, etc.). Tracked here so the exhaustiveness audit accounts for them rather than letting them fall through. A key is a case_id (every fail final of the case) or CASE:final (one final of a SOUND_ROW case that its row does not reach; docs/tech-debt.md TD-42). A deferral must be its final's only account. Prefer fixing over deferring.

cases.ARP_33:udp_eth_dst_is_mac1_not_mac2: The DUT's own behaviour is nondeterministic under CPU load, so this case cannot carry a row for BOTH of its fail finals -- and the two rows are each other's failure mode. ARP_33 injects TWO gratuitous Responses; whether the Linux DUT merges the second MAC depends on arp_is_garp/locktime timing, and under a loaded runner it sometimes keeps MAC1. Measured 2026-09-26 (smoke run 36220640037): with rows for both finals, `ARP_33#1` returned fail:udp_eth_dst_is_mac1_not_mac2 where fail:udp_eth_dst_neither_mac1_nor_mac2 was authored -- the DUT had kept MAC1, which swaps which row is right. NOT reproducible locally (80 rows at --workers 4, 80/80 PASS), which is itself the finding: it needs the sustained load of a full CI job. Its ARP_35 sibling DOES carry both rows, because Response-then-REQUEST addresses the DUT and the merge is deterministic -- that is what the earlier entry meant by ARP_33 being 'the same wall, and harder'. The `timing_serial` axis does not apply: it selects cases measuring a strict inter-frame cadence (frame_delta_within_us), and this is a DUT-state race, not an interval. A deferral by the rule below -- the reason names the DUT (docs/tech-debt.md TD-53)

empty_note: This note is kept from the day the ledger briefly emptied (2026-09-26); the way it emptied is the useful part. Every entry it held was eventually opened by a measurement that contradicted its own reason, never by the work the reason asked for. Four of them said a final was unreachable by an expect flip: ARP_33 and ARP_35 said 'not by any single flip' (true -- neg_expect_overrides carries a second token, and multi-row carries the second final; TD-53), SOMEIPSRV_ONWIRE_01 said the graded fields ARE the addressed fields (true of the fields, false of the design -- they were one field nobody had split; TD-54), and SOMEIPSRV_RPC_18 said phase 1 could only be opened by weakening it (false -- phase 1 asks WHICH PEER, which is identity, not the expectation it had been pinned to; TD-55). So: before adding an entry here, check that the reason names a property of the SPEC or the DUT. If it names a property of this harness -- one row per case, one field doing two jobs, a guard pinned to the wrong surface -- it is a defect wearing a deferral's clothes, and belongs in docs/tech-debt.md instead.
